$comment: The nightly all-drivers sweep (android-nightly-drivers.yml): every instrumentation driver under android/app/src/androidTest/kotlin/app/zen/chromium, the shard (one emulator boot) it runs on and the environment its own workflow gives it, as one directory - this file the shards, one <id>.json per driver, skip.json the classes and workflows left out with their reasons (a driver of its own file so that two branches adding drivers do not collide). android-nightly-drivers.mjs reads the directory as one manifest (the matrix, the plan, the table) and android-nightly-drivers.test.mjs asserts every concrete *Demo class is either a driver here or in skip.json with a reason. Driver fields: id (its directory in the artifact; the file is named after it), order (its place in the shard's run, ascending; ties by id; a driver without one runs last, by id - omit it for a new driver), class / classes (the *Demo classes it covers), shard, mirrors (the workflow file[:job or input] whose environment it takes), dir (DEMO_DIR, the handshake directory), script (a wrapper instead of android-gesture-demo.sh), out (where a script with a fixed output path leaves its findings, moved into the artifact), env (script-env lines), setup (named steps the shard runs before the emulator: see the runner), needs (pin, browser-role, navigation: state the runner sets or puts back), timeout (seconds for the driver, 720 by default), estimate (minutes, for the plan), note. Shard fields: cache (the path a setup step fills by a pin and the key naming that pin, kept between runs through the recipe's actions/cache inputs), setup, env, and each shard names its image (the SDK system image the recipe boots: system-images;android-<api-level>;<target>;x86_64, checked against those two) and its webview (the WebView provider the drivers run on: the image's own package and version, or what the shard's setup installs over it); both are printed in every run's header, the device's own word beside them.

phone-b.title: Phone B: API 34 Google APIs, pixel_6

phone-c.title: Phone C: API 34 Google APIs, pixel_6
phone-c.note: -camera-back emulated: the QR scan demo reads the emulated camera.

phone-d.title: Phone D: API 34 Google APIs, pixel_6

phone-e.title: Phone E: API 34 Google APIs, pixel_6
phone-e.note: The fifth phone shard (#344): the drivers the first four could not hold under about 58 minutes once every estimate was trued up to the minutes the nightly measured. Same recipe as phone-a.

phone-f.title: Phone F: API 34 Google APIs, pixel_6
phone-f.note: The sixth phone shard (W6-6, OS-37): the five before it stand at 66 to 68 of their 68 minutes, and the memory-pressure driver's five would fit on none of them. Same recipe as phone-a; the room for what wave 6 adds after it.

phone-g.title: Phone G: API 34 Google APIs, pixel_6
phone-g.note: The seventh phone shard (W6-H): the six before it stood at 64 to 68 of their 68 minutes and the last three merges each shuffled scenes by hand. Opened with a rebalance that leaves every phone shard at or under 58 minutes, a 10-minute headroom under the budget (nine drivers moved here, the largest movable of each shard; a driver a setup step, a first / last place or a sibling ties to its shard stayed). Same recipe as phone-a. The plan warns of any shard past 60 minutes (android-nightly-drivers.mjs check / estimate).

phone-h.title: Phone H: API 34 Google APIs, pixel_6
phone-h.note: The eighth phone shard (W6-S24c-b): phone-c and phone-g stood past the 60-minute headroom line (61.5 and 65.0 of their 68, once bookmarks-sort-view and sync-webdav had landed on them) and no other phone shard had the room for their drivers (57.5 to 60 each). Opened with seven drivers off those two alone – the largest of each that no camera, setup step, sibling, first or last place or perf series ties to its shard – leaving phone-c at 44.0, phone-g at 42.0 and this shard at 40.5: the room for what comes after. Same recipe as phone-a. api35 and webview stay past the line: their drivers are bound to their images, a second shard of each is the day's question when a driver next lands there.

api35-b.title: Phone, API 35 Google APIs, pixel_6 (B)
api35-b.note: The second API 35 shard (services pass 17, seed #36): api35 stood at 65.5 of its 68 minutes, past the 60-minute headroom line, and its drivers are bound to the image (the predictive back, the sheet leave and recede, the wake and status bar want API 35; the perf readings their baselines' WebView 124). Opened with the two profiling drivers alone, motion-perf and menu-perf (31.5 minutes, the two largest and the only two whose findings are traces and frame statistics rather than scenes), leaving the eight functional drivers on api35 at 34.0: the boot the profiles are read on carries no other driver's history before them, nearer the dispatch workflows' own boots their baselines were taken on. Same recipe as api35, the setup steps included (the shard's own list and the drivers' are the same two).

api33.title: Phone, API 33 Google APIs, pixel_6
api33.webview: com.google.android.webview 145.0.7632.218 installed over the image's 109.0.5414.123 (android-webview-google.sh: the APK out of Google's system-images;android-37.0;google_apis;x86_64 r6, the same signer)
api33.note: Android 13, the last version on which the browser's own share panel stands in for the system sheet (SH-03; Share.panelStandsIn): the share demo's panel scenes run here, its system-sheet scenes on phone-b. Same recipe as phone-a otherwise. The image's own WebView 109 keeps no profiles (no private tabs, the share demo's private check N/A – seed 69), so the setup installs a current Google WebView over it; the cache keeps that APK between runs.

webview.title: AOSP image (-writable-system) with the Chromium snapshot WebView swapped in
webview.webview: com.android.webview, the Chromium snapshot's SystemWebView swapped in (AndroidDesktop_x64 LAST_CHANGE at run time; the revision in webview-REVISIONS.json)
webview.note: swiftshader_indirect as the AOSP jobs ask (android-private-demo.yml: swangle draws a chrome frame every 1.3-3.5 s on this image); -camera-back emulated for the fullscreen demo, kept after that demo moved to webview-b (services pass 17, seed #36) so that the two snapshot-WebView phone shards boot one recipe. The private surfaces stay here: the private tabs, lock and security demos, the primitives' veil and the fakebox morph's private act.

webview-b.title: AOSP image (-writable-system) with the Chromium snapshot WebView swapped in (B)
webview-b.webview: com.android.webview, the Chromium snapshot's SystemWebView swapped in (AndroidDesktop_x64 LAST_CHANGE at run time; the revision in webview-REVISIONS.json)
webview-b.note: The second snapshot-WebView phone shard (services pass 17, seed #36): webview stood at 67.0 of its 68 minutes, past the 60-minute headroom line, and its drivers are bound to the swapped-in WebView (profiles for the private surfaces, a current engine for the media and notification behaviour). Opened with the media drivers – media, media-ui, pip and fullscreen, the four on the media-demo handshake (29 minutes) – and a11y-chrome-private (4, the private scene alone, which nothing ties to the other shard), 33.0 here against 34.0 left on webview. Same recipe as webview: the snapshot fetched by the setup step and swapped in by the first driver's prepare step (WEBVIEW_APK in this shard's env; a driver that blanks it, as ntp-morph-private does, must not run first on a shard), -camera-back emulated for the fullscreen demo.

tablet.title: Tablet: API 34 Google APIs, pixel_tablet at 1280x800@160

tablet-webview.title: Tablet on the AOSP image (-writable-system) with the Chromium snapshot WebView swapped in, pixel_tablet at 1280x800@160
tablet-webview.webview: com.android.webview, the Chromium snapshot's SystemWebView swapped in (AndroidDesktop_x64 LAST_CHANGE at run time; the revision in webview-REVISIONS.json)
tablet-webview.note: The tablet layout on the private tabs demos' engine (android-tablet-private-demo.yml): private tabs need WebViewFeature.MULTI_PROFILE, which the Google APIs image's WebView 113 lacks, so the tablet's private mode runs on the AOSP image with the snapshot WebView, under swiftshader_indirect as the webview shard.
